The agent's physics simulation diverged from the reference due to chaotic sensitivity to initial velocity/collision parameters, making the 0.0 outcome a fair reflection of output quality

outcome_detail: Agent produced a valid 18s video with correct duration (60/60 sampled frames matched), but mean SSIM of 0.6849 fell below the 0.70 gate threshold. Early frames (1-10) matched closely (pixel diff 3-15) but collision physics divergence caused large positional errors from frame 20+.
strategy: Analyze reference frames, extract positions/velocities, simulate bouncing physics in Revideo
agent_behavior: Extracted all 433 reference frames and used scipy ndimage to identify 12 colored ~52x52 squares on black background
Computed initial positions and velocities via color-matched tracking across frames with linear regression
Read Revideo documentation for signals, tweens, and linear easing before writing the scene
Built a frame-by-frame physics simulation with wall reflection and AABB elastic collisions
Iterated 7+ times on velocity parameters, wall bounds (inset 22 vs 26), and collision logic
Identified that default easing was non-linear and fixed to linear — a key debugging step
Recognized that collision physics are chaotic and small parameter errors compound, but ran out of improvement options
Submitted after ~30 minutes with the best achievable result given the approach
